chapter: Midwest bands: Hardy Brothers, Helvey and Buffalo
title: Why the kid band mattered: reading and learning together
summary: Leaders wanted musicians who could read, and the community band, unlike private lessons, taught reading and let kids learn from each other, which he says was the greatest thing that happened to him.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well, did you go and jam in those towns so they could hear you blow?
Yeah, sometimes you'd go out and jam, but they very seldom asked you about it, you know, because you -- even if the leader wasn't there, some of the guys would tell him, you know.
They can read, and they can play too, you know. You always wanted -- you were looking in them days for somebody to read, make sure they could read, you know.
Because you found a lot of trumpets, found a lot of any kind of musicians around but they wasn't -- they were self-taught, you know.
Well, that's why the kid band was so important.

Yeah, that's why it was such a background, sure. It was everything to me. I never could have did it without that. Because with a private teacher you don't get what you get from that. With a private teacher he takes you and you never know how you sound and you get disgusted, you know.
But with that band, with all these kids
in there, you're having fun, and also playing the music. And you're learning, you're showing each other things, you know.
